description: Curated source-dated winter 2025–26 harbor records across Superior and Sturgeon Bay. Sample, not an exhaustive fleet or current AIS tracker; lower-confidence records explicitly labeled.

harbors.name: Superior, Wisconsin
harbors.note: Map marker identifies the Superior harbor area only. Individual docks are listed in each vessel record; no vessel is placed at an invented berth coordinate.

harbors.name: Sturgeon Bay, Wisconsin
harbors.note: Harbor-wide reference near Sturgeon Bay. Vessel dry-dock positions and private shipyard access are NOT represented by map coordinates; berths can change during maintenance.

seasons.label: Winter 2026–27
seasons.note: The 2026–27 layup season is not yet confirmed in this registry. Do not inherit last winter's locations.

seasons.label: Winter 2025–26
seasons.note: Nine named historical layup records across Superior and Sturgeon Bay: eight supported by port authority or maritime historian, and one community-reported. These are a curated sample, NOT an exhaustive Great Lakes fleet roster. Individual source dates vary. Historical berth positions are never current locations.

evidence.title: Duluth Seaway Port Authority — Winter layup roster

records.name: Burns Harbor
records.summary: The 2025–26 port roster places Burns Harbor at Elevator M rather than at a shipyard. A winter berth does not establish that any particular repairs were scheduled.

events.text: Listed at Redwood Group Elevator M in Superior's winter layup roster.

evidence.title: Duluth Seaway Port Authority — Winter layup roster

records.name: Honorable James L. Oberstar
records.summary: The port lists the Oberstar among the vessels wintering at Fraser. Harbor camera reporting documents its departure on March 23, 2026, the first outbound vessel that spring.

events.text: Listed at Fraser Shipyards for winter 2025–26.
Duluth Harbor Cam reported the Oberstar departing as the first ship out of port that spring.

evidence.title: Duluth Seaway Port Authority — Winter layup roster

records.name: Indiana Harbor
records.summary: Indiana Harbor spent the documented layup at Ogdensburg Pier in Superior. This is a verified berth, not a claim of a specific overhaul or scheduled sailing date.

events.text: Listed at Ogdensburg Pier for winter layup.

evidence.title: Duluth Seaway Port Authority — Winter layup roster

records.name: John J. Boland
records.summary: The port's verified January roster places John J. Boland at Fraser Shipyards. The specific scope of vessel work remains unconfirmed here.

events.text: Listed at Fraser Shipyards for winter layup.

evidence.title: Duluth Seaway Port Authority — Winter layup roster

records.name: Lee A. Tregurtha
records.summary: Built in 1942 as a Navy tanker, Lee A. Tregurtha served during World War II before its Great Lakes career. Duluth Harbor Cam recorded its arrival for Fraser winter layup on January 16, 2026.

events.text: Duluth Harbor Cam documented arrival for winter layup at Fraser Shipyards.
Confirmed at Fraser Shipyards in the port's winter roster.
Duluth Harbor Cam reported a loaded departure through ice on Lake Superior.

photo.creator: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Detroit District
photo.alt: Lee A. Tregurtha transiting the Soo Locks in a 2021 photograph; not a winter layup image.

evidence.title: Duluth Seaway Port Authority — Winter layup roster

records.name: Mesabi Miner
records.summary: Fraser Shipyards described winter 2025–26 as Mesabi Miner's first winter layup at its Superior yard. MPR reported the ship moving across the harbor March 22, 2026, to load iron ore for Cleveland.

events.text: Shipyard reported this was Mesabi Miner's first winter layup at Fraser.
Confirmed at Fraser Shipyards on the port's winter roster.
MPR reported the vessel moved from its layup dock to load iron ore pellets in Duluth.

photo.creator: Tony Webster
photo.alt: Mesabi Miner sailing on Lake Superior in September 2018; not a winter layup photograph.

records.name: James R. Barker
records.berth: Fincantieri Bay Shipbuilding — graving dock on Jan 5
records.summary: One thousand feet of lake freighter came through ice into Sturgeon Bay on January 5, assisted by four tugs. The historical society reports the Barker entered the shipyard's large graving dock for winter storage, a five-year inspection and painting. Later shipyard movements are distinct dated events, not assumed continuing dock occupancy.

evidence.title: JAMES R. BARKER arrives at Fincantieri

events.text: Arrived at Sturgeon Bay with tug assistance; entered the Fincantieri graving dock for winter storage and five-year inspection.
Community port observers reported the Barker leaving its winter berth with tug and Coast Guard assistance.

storyFacts.text: Launched in 1976; the first thousand-foot Great Lakes ship built with its wheelhouse aft.

records.name: Edgar B. Speer
records.berth: Fincantieri Bay Shipbuilding — dock not independently verified
records.summary: On January 18, the Speer pivoted at the entrance to Sturgeon Bay and backed toward Bay Shipbuilding with two tugs assisting. Unlike most thousand-footers, its unloading equipment works sideways near the stern; that specialized arrangement shapes the ports it can serve.

evidence.title: EDGAR B. SPEER arrives at Fincantieri

events.text: Arrived at Fincantieri Bay Shipbuilding assisted by tugs Nickelena and Erika Kobasic.
Community observer reported a shift into the large graving dock. This is not an official berth assignment.

storyFacts.text: Launched in 1980 and known for its unusual 52-foot transverse unloading boom.
In 2006, assisted the Roger Blough after a rudder failure on the St. Marys River.

records.name: Manitoulin
records.berth: Fincantieri Bay Shipbuilding — specific berth unverified
records.summary: Multiple local shipping observers reported Manitoulin wintering at Sturgeon Bay in January 2026. Later discussion described a mid-February move into the graving dock. These are community observations, not a published shipyard berth roster; the specific position remains unverified.

evidence.title: BoatNerd community reports — Sturgeon Bay activity in winter 2026

events.text: Community observers reported Manitoulin arriving for layup in Sturgeon Bay; dock assignment not verified.
A subsequent community discussion described Manitoulin entering the shipyard's graving dock.

storyFacts.text: Its reported winter shifts show why a winter layup is a series of changing yard events rather than one fixed berth.
